scope: Proposition 6.15 (The exact XY activity calculus) of the manuscript “BKT universality for height and planar spin fields” (preprints/BKT-universality-for-height-and-planar-spin-fields-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e6a8df09e021c4a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 104-105. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the covariance construction and the local partition map above. Choose the fixed support and collar clearances, small-support threshold, and K0 first; then choose sufficiently large dyadic L, the polymer weight as in Proposition 4.8, a sufficiently small parameter neighborhood, and finally sufficiently large b. Within Equation (6.5) the original XY integrals admit positive representation sizes with all the following properties. Write sX(R) for the size of a specified representation on X, and ∥R∥A = supX A|X|sX(R). (i) An Fb leaf costs C/b; a nonzero charge q costs Ce−cbq2 , summable over q ̸= 0; the linear microscopic compensation costs C|s•|, and its nonlinear remainder costs C|s•|2. A full- block tensor costs C|t|, and a localized polynomial costs a constant times its coefficient on normalized m-scale directions. (ii) Convolving a compatible product multiplies its input sizes, up to a fixed factor per input. Temporary exclusions, relocation, scalar normalizer decorations, and separation into a single- ton tensor and remainder are exact. The animal and placement sums obey Proposition 4.8; hence all multiple-input and normalizer corrections are quadratic in the input sizes. 104 (iii) For a small single neutral linear input of size u, localization has normalized coefficients at most Cu and remainder size CL−3u in the even bulk after constant and quadratic subtraction, CL−2u at an even wall after constant subtraction, and CL−1u at a defect after constant subtraction. Each small charged single-input step has size at most CL−4u. Constants in these local gains do not grow with sufficiently large L. (iv) Sizes bound terminated evaluations and fixed-order Cauchy derivatives with bounded smooth normalized backgrounds. In finitely many normalized source directions the evaluated expres- sions are jointly holomorphic on fixed bounded polydiscs, with the corresponding Cauchy bounds after adding their finitely many probe events. They apply to copied good pieces, their one-time translations to defects, and the intrinsic offsets of Equation (6.7). For fixed separated sources, the lower bound on b is independent of their number; only the boundedly many late numerical event costs may depend on the fixed source configuration. If TΛ is an admissible early transport of an untagged representation, then for any AU ≥ AD > 0, before support relocation sX(TΛR) = sX(R), A |X| D sX(TΛR) ≤ (AD/AU )|X| ∥R∥AU . The transport leaves every opaque completed coefficient occurrence unchanged and is not defined on an already tagged live root. (v) Every finite-depth activity, assigned coefficient, and normalized partition identity is continuous in the permitted parameters, including at s = d∗s2 12 and at s = 0, as long as its scalar normalizers are nonzero. The statement holds on the plane at finite support, on finite reflected grids, and on auxiliary tori with terminal transverse harmonic directions. The bulk tensor and its local recursion are the same in all these settings wherever the calculation has the required clearance.
